dedupe_keys.name: oil tank detection dataset satellite images with oil storage tank annotations

description: The Oil Tank Detection Dataset is a benchmark for detecting oil storage tanks in satellite images with deep learning. It was presented in 2024 by Adel Chehade and Mostafa Rizk in an IEEE Access paper and a conference paper on YOLO models, and the Zenodo record was last updated in February 2026. It contains 12,948 satellite images with 171,809 bounding-box annotations of a single class, oil storage tank: 2,090 high-resolution Google Earth images annotated by hand with CVAT, plus three public data sets converted to YOLO format, refined and extended. Coverage is image tiles from locations that the abstract does not list, not a complete inventory. The data are one zipped archive of about 1.6 GB, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost, with code on GitHub. Caveats: images come partly from Google Earth and from third-party sets whose own terms may apply, and there are no tank attributes such as capacity. Simulation uses are training models to map fuel storage tanks for exposure analysis of fuel depots and terminals to floods, storm surge and fire. Related records: data-alberta-wells-satellite-dataset is a similar benchmark for oil and gas wells.
